definitions.gloss: Buddhist sutra; Buddhist scripture; chanting of sutras
definitions.explanation: Sacred Buddhist texts that are chanted during religious ceremonies, funerals, and memorial services. The お prefix adds a respectful or familiar tone.

examples.japanese: お{坊|ぼう}さんがお{経|きょう}を{読|よ}んでいる。
examples.english: The monk is chanting a sutra.

examples.japanese: {法事|ほうじ}でお{経|きょう}を{上|あ}げてもらった。
examples.english: We had a sutra chanted at the memorial service.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{仏壇|ぶつだん}の{前|まえ}でお{経|きょう}を{唱|とな}えている。
examples.english: My grandmother chants sutras in front of the Buddhist altar every morning.

notes:
USAGE:
The お prefix is standard and almost always used in everyday speech. The plain form {経|きょう} alone is more formal or literary. The most common verbs used with お{経|きょう} are {読|よ}む (to read/chant), {上|あ}げる (to offer up), and {唱|とな}える (to recite).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{経|きょう}を{読|よ}む (to chant a sutra)
- お{経|きょう}を{上|あ}げる (to offer sutra chanting)
- お{経|きょう}を{唱|とな}える (to recite a sutra)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Sutra chanting is central to Japanese Buddhist funerals and memorial services. Even families who are not actively religious typically have sutras chanted by a monk at funerals ({葬儀|そうぎ}) and annual memorial services ({法事|ほうじ}).
